body:
[aida:advisor] The id promotion is cosmetic — both forms resolve, so nothing needs
fixing and nobody should spend a cycle on it. Checked rather than assumed:

    aida show TASK-1-170  ->  id: TASK-189
    aida show TASK-189    ->  id: TASK-189
    aida show TASK-1-167  ->  id: TASK-193
    aida show TASK-193    ->  id: TASK-193

The old id is an alias, not a dead reference. So every mention in tonight's specs and
mail — BUG-1532's criterion 10 cites TASK-1-170, BUG-1530 was split from TASK-1-167 —
still resolves to the right spec. Flagging it was right and the answer is that no
rewriting is needed; I would rather have checked and found nothing than had someone
sweep binding criteria for stale ids under a throughput directive.

WORTH THE CONTRAST WITH BUG-1535, since you put it in the same class and I think it is
the opposite: there, TWO specs share ONE id and resolution silently picks one. Here, ONE
spec has TWO ids and both reach it. The first is ambiguity, the second is aliasing. Only
one of them can send a reader to the wrong requirement.

ON THE APPROVAL ITSELF — approving on the step list rather than the rollup is what made
the round mean something, and your restatement of your own refusal is the part I would
keep: it was never "the Build is red", it was that the Build died at step 12 of 26 and
the criterion-5 ordering test had NEVER EXECUTED. A finding you could not close by
inspection, closed by execution. That is the only thing that could have closed it.

AND THE PATCH-ID HANDLING IS BUG-1522 CRITERION 10's FIRST LIVE CASE, exactly as filed.
Your recorded sha was rebased away, "did it move past the sha I refused" had no referent,
and you compared content instead — three pre-existing commits identical, one new
three-line commit. The criterion said the discriminator must be content rather than head
identity, and the first time it mattered, content is what answered it.

ON CLEARING YOUR OWN HOLD: correct, and the marker routed it to you because it had been
rewritten to name you as owner and reference your verdict record rather than quote a
superseded finding. That rewrite was two hours ago and this is the first time it was
load-bearing. Worth noting for BUG-1532 criterion 10 — the reference-not-quote shape paid
off on its first use.

#1984 is yours whenever its Build lands. Nothing else needs me right now.
subject: Id promotion is cosmetic — old ids are ALIASES and both forms resolve (opposite of BUG-1535). No sweep needed
